name: Joy Kumar Ghosh
bio: Computer Science graduate (Magna Cum Laude, CGPA 3.77/4.00) from North South University, with a research focus on quantum information and secure communication. First author of an accepted manuscript in APL Quantum on a hybrid quantum key distribution protocol, achieving a 43.67% improvement in key-generation rate over the baseline. Seeking graduate study opportunities in quantum cryptography, quantum key distribution, and quantum computing.

researchInterests.title: Quantum Cryptography
researchInterests.description: Exploring cryptographic protocols leveraging quantum mechanical principles to achieve provably secure communication systems.

researchInterests.title: Quantum Key Distribution
researchInterests.description: Designing and optimizing QKD protocols for efficient and secure key exchange, including hybrid architectures like GHZ-BB84.

researchInterests.title: Quantum Computing
researchInterests.description: Investigating quantum circuit simulation, noise mitigation, and computational speedup using frameworks like Qiskit and PennyLane.

researchInterests.title: Quantum Communication
researchInterests.description: Studying quantum channels and protocols for secure, high-fidelity information transfer across quantum networks.

education.degree: B.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering

honorsAwards.title: Magna Cum Laude
honorsAwards.description: Awarded for graduating with a CGPA of 3.77/4.00, placing in the top tier of the graduating class.
